alex_sales: Heads-up — Acme wants the POC fully shut down by EOD Friday. Need a concise, actionable checklist for Hosted API keys, Dedicated pools, Private/VPC bits, and what to archive vs permanently delete. Who can own each step?

mike_se: I can own the hosted + dedicated parts. Quick plan: revoke hosted API keys, snapshot usage logs, drain dedicated pool (scale down + wait for in-flight requests), then release capacity. For private/VPC we need ops.

sophie_security: Add legal hold check first: confirm no outstanding e-discovery/legal requests. If legal hold = yes, we must preserve a copy of logs and model inputs for the hold period. If no, follow retention below.

jess_ops: I'll take the VPC teardown and storage retention tasks. Drafting checklist below — short items we can run as playbook.

alex_sales: perfect. paste the checklist here and we'll assign owners to each line so the customer gets a concrete timeline.

mike_se: Hosted API keys (owner: mike_se)
- Revoke all Acme API tokens through the Admin UI + force re-issue on their side.
- Export last 90 days of request logs to S3 (s3://redwood-exports/acme-poc/requests-YYYYMMDD).
- Mark token revocation in audit logs.
Command (curl example to invalidate a key):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/keys/revoke \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"key_id":"ak_ACME_12345","reason":"POC teardown"}'
```

Dedicated pool (owner: mike_se)
- Set pool to drain mode: prevents new allocations.
- Wait for active sessions to drop to 0 (max wait 30m), then scale to 0.
- Export runtime metrics and KV cache stats (for debugging) to same S3 folder.
- Release GPU quota (ops action) and tag pool as decommissioned.
CLI snippet to drain and scale:```\nredwoodctl pools drain --id pool-6789 --timeout 1800\nredwoodctl pools scale --id pool-6789 --replicas 0
```

sophie_security: Data retention rules (owner: sophie_security)
- PII: delete any user-level PII within 7 days unless legal hold.
- Model inputs/outputs: retain for 30 days by default, move to cold storage for 90 days if needed for quality reviews, then delete.
- Audit logs: keep for 365 days in WORM (write-once) archive unless legal hold.
- Evidence of deletion: create and store a deletion manifest with object hashes and timestamps.

jess_ops: Private / VPC teardown (owner: jess_ops)
- Remove customer VPC peering and BGP routes once traffic is drained.
- Revoke firewall rules and remove any NAT/gateway resources allocated for the POC.
- If on-prem: coordinate with customer ops for host deprovision and hardware wipe.
- Snapshot attached volumes and export to S3 archive if retention required; otherwise schedule secure wipe.
- Update infra ticket with links to snapshots + deletion manifests.
Commands (internal):
```
# revoke peering
redwoodctl vpc peering delete --peering-id pcx-abc123 --confirm
# snapshot volumes
redwoodctl volumes snapshot --filter tag:acme-poc --out s3://redwood-exports/acme-poc/vol-snapshots/
```

mike_se: Additional ops notes:
- Cache eviction: clear any prefix/KV caches associated with the POC to avoid old artifacts being served to other tenants.
- Model variants: un-assign any canary routing rules pointing at Acme-specific variants.
CLI: ``redwoodctl cache flush --scope acme-poc``

sophie_security: Legal hold / compliance checklist:
- Confirm PO lifecycle status with legal: alex_sales please confirm if legal hold needed.
- If legal hold = yes: set retention_tag=legalhold and move artifacts to secure bucket with restricted IAM.
- If no: follow the deletion schedule above and produce manifest.

alex_sales: Legal says no hold for now. Please proceed with standard retention/deletion timeline.

jess_ops: Scheduling: I'll run the hosted key revocation + log export at 10:00 PDT Thursday, drain dedicated pool at 11:00 PDT, then VPC teardown window at 13:00 PDT. Ops will produce deletion manifests by EOD Friday.

mike_se: I'll post confirmation messages at each step and paste links to the S3 exports. Also will run cache flush after pool scale-down.

jess_ops: decomm-bot — please schedule the automated sweep job for Friday 23:00 UTC so final deletes happen after business hours.

decomm-bot: Scheduled job created: acme-poc-final-sweep (job id: sweep-2026-03-27-772). Steps: revoke-keys -> export-logs -> drain-pool -> snapshot-volumes -> flush-cache -> delete-objects. Run window: 2026-03-27T23:00:00Z. :white_check_mark:

alex_sales: great — please add the list and times to the customer-facing email. i'll send an update to Acme now. thx all :pray:
